descriptors.R: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1921 to 1933
descriptors.D: nominee of the party in office since 1933, renominating the sitting President for a fourth term

compile_desc.R: the party that held the presidency from 1921 to 1933

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Socialist and a Prohibition nominee, and in Texas an unpledged slate of electors (answer "other").
never_name: Dewey, Roosevelt, Bricker, Truman, Wallace, Willkie, Norman Thomas, Claude Watson or Hoover

slice_sources.men: 1940 and 1950 censuses interpolated to November 1944; men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states, citizens only, including the millions in uniform who voted by state or federal absentee ballot; Black voters here vote heavily Democratic since 1936; calibrated to certified 1944 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1944, women 21+ outside the South, all enfranchised by the Nineteenth Amendment; turnout from the carried-forward women-to-men ratio, calibrated to each state's 1944 vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1944, white adults (Mexican-origin adults counted as white, as in 1940) in the eleven former Confederate states, 18+ in Georgia, which lowered its voting age to 18 in 1943; calibrated to certified 1944 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1944, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states (18+ in Georgia); Smith v. Allwright struck down the white primary in April 1944, but poll taxes and literacy tests keep most disfranchised, so the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1944, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized (Chinese immigrants became eligible to naturalize in 1943); no state let aliens vote.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
